clue.text: In fact, Magi may have been excited by words from Mary

indicators.note: something stirred up and excited is thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The Three Wise Men may have been thrilled by something the Virgin Mary said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may have been excited' rearranges the ten letters of IN FACT MAGI; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magnificat is the canticle sung by the Virgin Mary in Luke's gospel, so literally her words.

clue.text: Voice of loud gangster starting row

indicators.note: the row comes after the earlier pieces, which start it off

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
Al Capone, the Chicago gangster, gives AL
a set-to is a quarrel or row

explanation.surface: A noisy mobster's voice is heard as an argument begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starting' tells you the gangster and loudness come at the start, ahead of SET-TO, a British word for a fight or row.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsetto is a register of the singing or speaking voice above the natural range.

clue.text: At bottom of Greek valley find hard beans

indicators.note: in a down entry the hard letter sits at the foot, below the valley

parts.note: the Vale of Tempe is a famous valley in Thessaly
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A traveller finds hard beans growing at the foot of a valley in Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'At bottom of' puts H below TEMPE; 'find' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempeh is an Indonesian food made from fermented soya beans pressed into a cake.

clue.text: Again conceals a one-sided tendency

indicators.note: the word for again hides the next piece inside itself

parts.note: bis is a call for a repeat performance, meaning again or twice

explanation.surface: Something hides, once more, a partisan leaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conceals' puts the A inside BIS, the musical direction or encore call for a repeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Bias is a prejudice that leans one way, so a lopsided inclination fits it exactly.

clue.text: Wounded revolutionary protected by English lad — a symbol of honour?

indicators.note: the outer pieces wrap round the inner ones as a shield would

parts.note: a son is a boy or lad
cut means wounded by a blade
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: An injured rebel is shielded by an English boy, which might earn a badge of honour.
explanation.walkthrough: Che Guevara is the stock crossword revolutionary; 'protected by' means the English lad wraps round the wounded rebel. The question mark admits the definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: An escutcheon is the shield bearing a coat of arms, an emblem of family honour.

clue.text: Dish provided by king's decree

parts.note: Old King Cole of the nursery rhyme, with his possessive
a law is a decree

explanation.surface: A monarch rules by royal edict what food is served.
explanation.walkthrough: Old King Cole is the 'merry old soul' of the nursery rhyme; 'provided by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleslaw is a salad dish of shredded raw cabbage, usually in mayonnaise.

clue.text: Name of important family doctor coming before lunchtime?

indicators.note: the doctor is placed ahead of the next piece

parts.note: a medic is a doctor
one o'clock is lunchtime, and one is I in Roman numerals; the question mark flags the stretch

explanation.surface: The family GP drops in just before lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: Lunchtime is taken as one o'clock, and one is I as a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: The Medici were the powerful banking family who ruled Renaissance Florence.

clue.text: Woman's way to avoid extremes

indicators.note: the word for way loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a manner is a way of doing something

explanation.surface: A woman's approach is to steer clear of going too far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to avoid extremes' strips the first and last letters from MANNER; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne is a common female forename, and crosswords often define a name by its sex.

clue.text: Hardy trainee mostly in such schools

indicators.note: the shortened trainee goes inside the designer's surname

parts.note: Sir Hardy Amies was the British fashion designer and royal dressmaker

indicators.note: the word for trainee loses its final letter

parts.note: a cadet is a trainee, especially for the forces

explanation.surface: A tough recruit has nearly finished at some kind of school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy' looks like an adjective meaning tough, but it is the royal dressmaker Sir Hardy Amies; 'mostly' trims the trainee's last letter and 'in' puts the rest inside his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Academies are schools, such as military academies, the places where trainees are taught.

clue.text: 'Enry's bucket had this yellow liquid

indicators.note: a Cockney who says 'Enry for Henry drops his aitches, so the H goes

parts.note: in the folk song 'There's a Hole in My Bucket', the bucket has a hole in it

explanation.surface: Henry's leaky pail held some yellowish fluid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enry is Henry with the H dropped, as in a Cockney accent, so HOLE IN loses its H. The song 'There's a Hole in My Bucket' has a Henry in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Olein is a yellowish oily liquid, the glyceride of oleic acid found in fats.

clue.text: See 22 down
See 22 down
Fur makes female feel uncomfortable

parts.note: to itch is to feel an irritation on the skin

explanation.surface: A fur coat makes a woman scratch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' is a link between the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitch is the fur of the polecat, also called fitchew.

clue.text: One officer and another into weird music and spooky practices

parts.note: an OC is an officer commanding

indicators.note: the second officer is put inside the rearranged letters
weird music is music turned strange, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, a second officer

explanation.surface: Two officers get caught up in strange music and eerie goings-on.
explanation.walkthrough: OC (officer commanding) is a standard army abbreviation; the leading 'One' is just an article. 'weird' scrambles the music and 'into' sets the lieutenant inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Occultism is belief in and practice of the supernatural and magic, which is spooky stuff.

clue.text: Branch of lexicography soon in trouble — coming across something sticky?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters stretch across, round the sticky piece
a word in trouble is in disarray, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: mastic is a gum or resin used as an adhesive; the question mark admits the vagueness

explanation.surface: A dictionary department will soon be in difficulty when it meets something gummy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' scrambles soon to ONOS, and 'coming across' wraps those letters round the gum, the last S closing it off.
explanation.definitionFit: Onomastics is the study of proper names, a specialist field within lexicography.

clue.text: Try to do this as a music student — they'll give you many openings

definitions.text: Try to do this as a music student
definitions.meaning: a music student aims to gain full command of keys, the scales and harmonies
a key that fits many locks opens many doors

explanation.surface: Advice to a music student, followed by a promise of plenty of opportunities.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is a pun: a student tries to master the keys of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Master keys open every lock in a set, and to master keys is what a music student does.

clue.text: Act like a painstaking cruciverbalist and be tactful

definitions.meaning: a careful setter or solver picks every entry with great care
to be tactful is to speak with diplomacy and discretion

explanation.surface: Behave like a meticulous crossword setter and be diplomatic.
explanation.walkthrough: A cruciverbalist is a crossword setter or solver, who literally selects words with care.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to speak with tact, and a fussy setter literally selects words with care.

clue.text: I censor a terrible plot for stage work

indicators.note: a terrible piece of work is a mess, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A censor condemns an awful storyline for a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges the letters of I CENSOR A.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is the outline plot of a play, film or opera.

clue.text: Soldiers going to a heroic place of death heard bugle sound

parts.note: the RE are the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

indicators.note: heard means we want a word that is pronounced like the valley

parts.note: Tennyson's Light Brigade rode 'into the valley of Death'

explanation.surface: Troops riding to a glorious end hear a bugle call.
explanation.walkthrough: British speakers say the call 'ri-VAL-ee', so its ending sounds like 'valley' ('heard'); the valley is Tennyson's 'Charge of the Light Brigade'. 'going to a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Reveille is the bugle call that wakes soldiers in the morning.

clue.text: One brought in tenth possibly — to be put across counter in this?

definitions.text: One brought in tenth possibly — to be put across counter in this?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters with I are spread on either side of the counter
the numeral is taken inside the rearranged letters
possibly says the word could be rearranged into another order

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral
a bar is a counter, as in a pub

explanation.surface: A tenth of the harvest was carried in and laid on a counter in this building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' scrambles the tenth to make room for I ('brought in'), giving TITHEN; 'put across' spreads that round the counter. A tithe barn is where the church's tenth was stored.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe barn stored the tenth of produce paid to the church, so the whole clue describes one.

clue.text: Pacific fish god, venomous creature

parts.note: the tai is a red sea bream of Pacific waters
Pan is the Greek god of the wild

explanation.surface: A fish from the Pacific and a deity combine as a poisonous beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The taipan is a highly venomous Australian snake.

clue.text: Bank's reception

definitions.meaning: an embankment built along a river to stop flooding
a formal morning gathering of guests, once held by a monarch

explanation.surface: A financial institution's party.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link; it reads as a possessive, joining a bank to its reception.
explanation.definitionFit: A levee is a river embankment, and also a formal reception held by a sovereign.

clue.text: Stop decider losing initial power

indicators.note: the word for decider drops a letter

parts.note: a play-off is a deciding match after a tie

indicators.note: initial picks out the first letter of power

explanation.surface: A decisive match is halted after the first loss of strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes P, the first letter of 'power' (picked by 'initial'), out of PLAY-OFF.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay off something is to stop doing it, as in 'lay off the biscuits'.

clue.text: Around the edge, drag computer graphics files

indicators.note: the word for drag goes around the edge

parts.note: to cart is to drag or haul
a lip is an edge or rim

explanation.surface: Pull something round the border of a set of image files.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' puts the edge inside the word for drag; the surface sounds like dragging a file across a screen with a mouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Clip art is ready-made pictures supplied as files for use in documents.

clue.text: Nice pet pin-up ceases to be funny as work of surrealist art

indicators.note: to be funny is to be odd or peculiar, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A pin-up of a lovely pet stops being amusing as a piece of surrealism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be funny' rearranges all eighteen letters of NICE PET PIN-UP CEASES; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This French title, 'This is not a pipe', is written on Magritte's famous surrealist painting of a pipe.

clue.text: Spooner's fellow, bumpkin making a pile in the country

indicators.note: Spooner's tells you to swap the opening sounds of the two words

parts.note: Ray is a man's name, a fellow
a hick is a country bumpkin

explanation.surface: A yokel named Ray builds a heap out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening letters of RAY and HICK gives HAY and RICK; 'making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A hayrick is a haystack, a large pile of hay stacked out in a field.

clue.text: Fling with actress leaving you upset

indicators.note: the reversed word for you leaves the actress's name

parts.note: Elizabeth Hurley is a British actress

indicators.note: upset turns the word for you upside down, so in a down entry it reads backwards

parts.note: ye is an old word for you

explanation.surface: A romance with a film star leaves you distraught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses YE to EY, and 'leaving' takes EY from HURLEY; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To fling and to hurl both mean to throw something hard.
